pal_001: You can recognise it by the thicket of secondary trunks and aerial roots, grown into a colonnade measured at 36 metres round and 21 metres tall. It stands in the Giardino Garibaldi in the middle of Piazza Marina.
pal_002: You can recognise it by the messages, photographs and poems taped to the trunk, renewed every 23 May, on a fig only 2.91 metres round. It stands on the pavement outside the 1960s apartment block at Via Notarbartolo 23.
pal_003: You can recognise it by the 44 secondary trunks dropping from the branches and thickening into columns where they reach the ground, under a crown of some 3,000 square metres. It stands inside the ticketed Orto Botanico.
pal_004: You can recognise it by the tiered, umbrella-shaped crown, each segment ending in a burst of stiff blue green leaves, on a trunk 5.9 metres round. It stands in the garden, away from the house; the big fig is nearer that.
pal_005: You can recognise it by its girth, six metres round on a tree only seven metres tall, the largest of the group. They stand in front of the Palazzina Cinese, the Chinese pavilion in Parco della Favorita.
pal_006: You can recognise it by the trunk, nearly five metres round, the thickest of the roughly twenty figs planted on these grounds. It stands in the public park at Villa Trabia, the estate that now holds a library.
pal_007: You can recognise it by its trunk, up to 2.5 metres round, one of the mature survivors among the hundreds of date palms planted here in 1905. It stands in the unfenced garden of Villa Bonanno, facing the Norman Palace.
pal_008: You can recognise them by the colonnade of fan palms tall enough to shade the whole length of the entrance avenue. They line the Via Lincoln approach into Villa Giulia.
pal_009: You can recognise it by the long horizontal branches running out parallel to the ground, reading as a low green ceiling rather than a column. It stands closest to the house at Villa Malfitano; the dragon tree is elsewhere.
pal_010: You can recognise it by the shade it throws over half the Lago dei Cigni, on a trunk system 27.3 metres round and 30 metres tall. It stands at the swan lake in the Villa Tasca grounds, across the water from the plane tree.
pal_015: You can recognise it by the trunk, 8.2 metres round under a crown just 11 metres tall. It stands in the Giardino Inglese, the one of the park's several big figs that Sicily's monumental tree register measured.
pal_016: You can recognise it by the stone pine it has grown around and partly absorbed. It stands on the terraced garden atop the walls of the Palazzo dei Normanni, the largest of the three figs there at ten metres round.
pal_018: You can recognise it by the bare branches covered in small scarlet bells, in the years it flowers, on a trunk 4.5 metres round. It stands in the working nursery, 85 metres from the dragon tree at the same address.
pal_019: You can recognise it by the single trunk and one crown, 30 metres tall, where the fig beside the lake spreads into a colonnade instead. It stands 184 metres from that fig, on the far side of the Villa Tasca swan lake.
